quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7424:quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:81:| GAP-F-07 | `FormatTable` GC / compaction not implemented. Sparse format-overlay (Phase 4.5.D) interns format strings into a workbook-level `FormatTable`. When cells change format, the old `FormatId` entry is NOT garbage-collected. Long-lived workbooks that cycle through many formats grow the table. **Decision (W5-68 design doc § 7.5):** deferred — typical workbooks don't cycle formats; a compaction pass lands in Phase 4.10 or on explicit user request. | Filed at design time (W5-68); no code yet | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7425:quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

Acceptance: FN4-260-01 ✅ 260 registered; FN4-260-02 ✅ every fn has matrix-backed tests + coverage-discipline EXPLICITLY_DEFERRED entry; FN4-260-03 ✅ unregistered fns produce `#NAME?`. Per-batch audit-discipline rule (parallel Codex + separate-Opus) caught Codex 1H/2M/7L + Opus 5H/10M/20L across the 5 V1-260 closeout batches; all closed in-commit per the `.1` convention. **W5-D-13.1 phase megaudit** (2026-05-18, parallel Codex + Opus + self) caught 6 ADDITIONAL HIGH issues invisible at the per-batch level: 28 range-aware fns missing from `is_aggregate_function` binder admission (extending the W5-D-12 SUBTOTAL-only fix to the whole family), 3 fns unreachable from formula source text (ATAN2/SUMXMY2/DAYS360 — lexer letters>3+digit gap), `GAMMA.INV` finite-subnormal-scale panic (incomplete W5-D-5.1 closure), W5-D-12 closure shipped without recommended named-range e2e test, audit-discipline systemic blind spot for dispatch-path coverage, 21 fns in Date/Time + TRANSPOSE marked ❌ but registered (matrix-registry drift). All 6 HIGHs closed in W5-D-13.1. Known follow-ups (deferred, NOT regressions): (a) literal range refs in `AggregateArg` context (`SUM(A1:A10)`, `CORREL(A1:A4, B1:B4)`) remain unbindable — pre-existing engine-wide gap at `plan.rs:706-731` and `plan.rs:380-383`, affects EVERY aggregate not just Phase 4.10 fns; named-range and scalar-args paths work today via W5-D-13.1; (b) Batch E remainders LOOKUP vector form + LEFTB/RIGHTB/MIDB/LENB/FINDB/SEARCHB byte-length variants. Full audit trail: 24 per-batch transcripts at `docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-*.md` + 3 megaudit transcripts at `docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-{codex,opus,self}.md`.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:8139:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:868:quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:81:| GAP-F-07 | `FormatTable` GC / compaction not implemented. Sparse format-overlay (Phase 4.5.D) interns format strings into a workbook-level `FormatTable`. When cells change format, the old `FormatId` entry is NOT garbage-collected. Long-lived workbooks that cycle through many formats grow the table. **Decision (W5-68 design doc § 7.5):** deferred — typical workbooks don't cycle formats; a compaction pass lands in Phase 4.10 or on explicit user request. | Filed at design time (W5-68); no code yet | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:8140:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:869:quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

Path: W5-D-1..W5-D-7 Wave 3 distributions (+38 → 238), W5-D-8 BIT* (+5 → 243), W5-D-9 base conversion (+6 → 249), W5-D-10 ERF/ERFC family (+4 → 253), W5-D-11 PERCENTILE/QUARTILE (+6 → 259), W5-D-12 SUBTOTAL (+1 → **260** — V1-260 hit). 12 closeout-arc batches with ship+audit commit pairs each (24 audit transcript files: 1 Codex + 1 Opus per batch). Matrix coverage 82% post-W5-D-13.1 megaudit closure per `scripts/report-compat-coverage.sh`. Acceptance: FN4-260-01 ✅ 260 registered; FN4-260-02 ✅ every fn has matrix-backed tests + coverage-discipline EXPLICITLY_DEFERRED entry; FN4-260-03 ✅ unregistered fns produce `#NAME?`. All 6 HIGHs closed in W5-D-13.1. Known follow-ups (deferred, NOT regressions): (a) literal range refs in `AggregateArg` context (`SUM(A1:A10)`, `CORREL(A1:A4, B1:B4)`) remain unbindable — pre-existing engine-wide gap at `plan.rs:706-731` and `plan.rs:380-383`, affects EVERY aggregate not just Phase 4.10 fns; named-range and scalar-args paths work today via W5-D-13.1; (b) Batch E remainders LOOKUP vector form + LEFTB/RIGHTB/MIDB/LENB/FINDB/SEARCHB byte-length variants. Sparse format-overlay (Phase 4.5.D) interns format strings into a workbook-level `FormatTable`. When cells change format, the old `FormatId` entry is NOT garbage-collected. Long-lived workbooks that cycle through many formats grow the table. **Decision (W5-68 design doc § 7.5):** deferred — typical workbooks don't cycle formats; a compaction pass lands in Phase 4.10 or on explicit user request. | Filed at design time (W5-68); no code yet | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:8669:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1624:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:7357:    80	| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

Path: W5-D-1..W5-D-7 Wave 3 distributions (+38 → 238), W5-D-8 BIT* (+5 → 243), W5-D-9 base conversion (+6 → 249), W5-D-10 ERF/ERFC family (+4 → 253), W5-D-11 PERCENTILE/QUARTILE (+6 → 259), W5-D-12 SUBTOTAL (+1 → **260** — V1-260 hit). 12 closeout-arc batches with ship+audit commit pairs each (24 audit transcript files: 1 Codex + 1 Opus per batch). Matrix coverage 82% post-W5-D-13.1 megaudit closure per `scripts/report-compat-coverage.sh`. Acceptance: FN4-260-01 ✅ 260 registered; FN4-260-02 ✅ every fn has matrix-backed tests + coverage-discipline EXPLICITLY_DEFERRED entry; FN4-260-03 ✅ unregistered fns produce `#NAME?`. Per-batch audit-discipline rule (parallel Codex + separate-Opus) caught Codex 1H/2M/7L + Opus 5H/10M/20L across the 5 V1-260 closeout batches; all closed in-commit per the `.1` convention. **W5-D-13.1 phase megaudit** (2026-05-18, parallel Codex + Opus + self) caught 6 ADDITIONAL HIGH issues invisible at the per-batch level: 28 range-aware fns missing from `is_aggregate_function` binder admission (extending the W5-D-12 SUBTOTAL-only fix to the whole family), 3 fns unreachable from formula source text (ATAN2/SUMXMY2/DAYS360 — lexer letters>3+digit gap), `GAMMA.INV` finite-subnormal-scale panic (incomplete W5-D-5.1 closure), W5-D-12 closure shipped without recommended named-range e2e test, audit-discipline systemic blind spot for dispatch-path coverage, 21 fns in Date/Time + TRANSPOSE marked ❌ but registered (matrix-registry drift). All 6 HIGHs closed in W5-D-13.1. Known follow-ups (deferred, NOT regressions): (a) literal range refs in `AggregateArg` context (`SUM(A1:A10)`, `CORREL(A1:A4, B1:B4)`) remain unbindable — pre-existing engine-wide gap at `plan.rs:706-731` and `plan.rs:380-383`, affects EVERY aggregate not just Phase 4.10 fns; named-range and scalar-args paths work today via W5-D-13.1; (b) Batch E remainders LOOKUP vector form + LEFTB/RIGHTB/MIDB/LENB/FINDB/SEARCHB byte-length variants. Full audit trail: 24 per-batch transcripts at `docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-*.md` + 3 megaudit transcripts at `docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-{codex,opus,self}.md`.

Per-batch audit-discipline rule (parallel Codex + separate-Opus) caught Codex 1H/2M/7L + Opus 5H/10M/20L across the 5 V1-260 closeout batches; all closed in-commit per the `.1` convention. **W5-D-13.1 phase megaudit** (2026-05-18, parallel Codex + Opus + self) caught 6 ADDITIONAL HIGH issues invisible at the per-batch level: 28 range-aware fns missing from `is_aggregate_function` binder admission (extending the W5-D-12 SUBTOTAL-only fix to the whole family), 3 fns unreachable from formula source text (ATAN2/SUMXMY2/DAYS360 — lexer letters>3+digit gap), `GAMMA.INV` finite-subnormal-scale panic (incomplete W5-D-5.1 closure), W5-D-12 closure shipped without recommended named-range e2e test, audit-discipline systemic blind spot for dispatch-path coverage, 21 fns in Date/Time + TRANSPOSE marked ❌ but registered (matrix-registry drift). All 6 HIGHs closed in W5-D-13.1. Known follow-ups (deferred, NOT regressions): (a) literal range refs in `AggregateArg` context (`SUM(A1:A10)`, `CORREL(A1:A4, B1:B4)`) remain unbindable — pre-existing engine-wide gap at `plan.rs:706-731` and `plan.rs:380-383`, affects EVERY aggregate not just Phase 4.10 fns; named-range and scalar-args paths work today via W5-D-13.1; (b) Batch E remainders LOOKUP vector form + LEFTB/RIGHTB/MIDB/LENB/FINDB/SEARCHB byte-length variants. Full audit trail: 24 per-batch transcripts at `docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-*.md` + 3 megaudit transcripts at `docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-{codex,opus,self}.md`.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:10092:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v2-v1-codex.md:3049: | GAP-F-07 | `FormatTable` GC / compaction not implemented. Sparse format-overlay (Phase 4.5.D) interns format strings into a workbook-level `FormatTable`. When cells change format, the old `FormatId` entry is NOT garbage-collected. Long-lived workbooks that cycle through many formats grow the table. **Decision (W5-68 design doc § 7.5):** deferred — typical workbooks don't cycle formats; a compaction pass lands in Phase 4.10 or on explicit user request. | Filed at design time (W5-68); no code yet | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:10093:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v2-v1-codex.md:3051: | GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-7-codex.md:8418:docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:177:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-wave-2-closing-megaudit-codex.md:8121:docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:125:| CEILING.MATH | ✅ | 7 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. CEILING.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |

(mirrors FLOOR canon, diverges from CEILING.MATH). FLOOR.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3628:docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:4342:docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:623:./docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:621:./docs/known-gaps.md:81:| GAP-F-07 | `FormatTable` GC / compaction not implemented. Sparse format-overlay (Phase 4.5.D) interns format strings into a workbook-level `FormatTable`. When cells change format, the old `FormatId` entry is NOT garbage-collected. Long-lived workbooks that cycle through many formats grow the table. **Decision (W5-68 design doc § 7.5):** deferred — typical workbooks don't cycle formats; a compaction pass lands in Phase 4.10 or on explicit user request. | Filed at design time (W5-68); no code yet | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 |

Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:657:./docs/phase2/exit-packet.md:12:This packet closes Phase 2A of the Quantbook engine. Phase 2A shipped five feature items (2A.1, 2A.2, 2A.4, 2A.5, and the deferred-from-Phase-1 H6 work in 2A.7) plus a complete megaudit cycle (2A.6 + 2A.7-.13) — the audit's findings drove most of the substantive correctness work.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:685:./docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:186:| 12 | **4.9.L** (W5-148, shipped) | Round-trip + edge case verification suite. +12 end-to-end property tests in `workbook_runtime::tests`: mixed-relativity range rejection at set_formula, `Sales[@Col]` vs `@Sales[Qty]` semantic equivalence, `@A:A` / `@1:1` whole-range narrowing at anchor, `Sheet1!@A1` cross-sheet, R1C1+EN round-trip through op-log replay (set_reference_mode + set_formula both replayed), DE+EN round-trip through replay, `@` preservation through replay, reference_mode/locale changes leave stored text canonical, `@scalar` idempotency, `@SUM(scalar args)` no-op. Note: rule 7 (function-returns-array → top-left) deferred — array-returning functions in scalar context still return `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit; closing megaudit (4.9.O) decides whether to bundle that with cell-boundary spill rewiring or defer to a Phase 4.10 polish item. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:784:./docs/architecture/2026-05-14-array-formulas-and-spills.md:602:**v1 scope (post-W5-108 / Phase 4.7.O closure update):** 1D inputs only — `array` and `include` must both be row vectors (1×N) or both column vectors (N×1), with matching length. 2D inputs (N×M array + N×1 or 1×M mask) deferred to v2 / Phase 4.10. The shipped implementation at `crates/ql-functions/src/array_returning_fns.rs:335-341` rejects any `array` with `rows > 1 AND cols > 1` with `#VALUE!`. The 2D enumeration below describes the eventual target shape; do NOT take it as the shipped 4.7 scope.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:815:./docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2166:docs/architecture/2026-05-13-dates-times-formats.md:365:When cells change format, the old FormatId entry isn't garbage-collected. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:821:./docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2271:docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.5-megaudit-sonnet.md:171:365.25 divisor; full Excel basis-1 algorithm deferred to Phase 4.10."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:822:./docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2288:docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:123:| CEILING.MATH | ✅ | 7 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. CEILING.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:823:./docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2289:docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:124:| FLOOR.MATH | ✅ | 8 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Mirror of CEILING.MATH. Positive number rounds toward -∞; negative+mode=0 toward -∞ (away from zero); negative+mode≠0 toward +∞ (toward zero). significance=0 + nonzero number → #DIV/0! (mirrors FLOOR canon, diverges from CEILING.MATH). FLOOR.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |

Provenance-aware dispatch is deferred. | 🟢 errors / 🟡 direct-args | `count_skips_errors_canon`, `count_skips_text_and_bools_v1_divergence`, `count_direct_bool_and_numeric_text_v1_divergence` |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1257:./docs/audits/2026-05-13-finalization-planning-codex.txt:806:   158	| CONCAT | ❌ | 0 | 4.10 | Range-aware variant of CONCATENATE — deferred to wave 2 (needs RangeAwareFn flatten). |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1318:./docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:123:| CEILING.MATH | ✅ | 7 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. CEILING.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1319:./docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:124:| FLOOR.MATH | ✅ | 8 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Mirror of CEILING.MATH. Positive number rounds toward -∞; negative+mode=0 toward -∞ (away from zero); negative+mode≠0 toward +∞ (toward zero). significance=0 + nonzero number → #DIV/0! (mirrors FLOOR canon, diverges from CEILING.MATH). FLOOR.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1556:./docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:7357:    80	| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1883:123:| CEILING.MATH | ✅ | 7 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. CEILING.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:1884:124:| FLOOR.MATH | ✅ | 8 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Mirror of CEILING.MATH. Positive number rounds toward -∞; negative+mode=0 toward -∞ (away from zero); negative+mode≠0 toward +∞ (toward zero). significance=0 + nonzero number → #DIV/0! (mirrors FLOOR canon, diverges from CEILING.MATH). FLOOR.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2288:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-2-opus.md:377:**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM because the gap is "drift between matcher (pre-lists 7) and registry (4 registered, 3 deferred) not pinned." The Step 1 matcher-pin test pins matcher correctness; the Step 2 test pins disjointness for Step-2 fns. The triangulation of "matcher recognizes 7, registry has 4, none of the other 3 are leaked into other tiers" isn't pinned anywhere. A future contributor who pre-registers ISFORMULA as scalar (for testing) would not get caught by any existing test until Step 3 lands.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2444:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:606:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.F-codex-review.txt:6618:9. PASS with future-test requirement: The current cell-boundary interim state is sound because the spill path is explicitly deferred and `WorkbookRuntime::set_formula` still routes root formulas through scalar eval at `crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime.rs:524`. In 4.7.J, root array/spill detection must intercept before those eval calls; otherwise the failure mode is visible `#CALC!`, not silent scalar truncation. Add runtime tests for `={1,2}` at a cell root spilling rather than returning `#CALC!`.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3383:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:606:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.F-codex-review.txt:6618:9. PASS with future-test requirement: The current cell-boundary interim state is sound because the spill path is explicitly deferred and `WorkbookRuntime::set_formula` still routes root formulas through scalar eval at `crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime.rs:524`. Add runtime tests for `={1,2}` at a cell root spilling rather than returning `#CALC!`.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3560:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:938:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-2-opus.md:377:**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM because the gap is "drift between matcher (pre-lists 7) and registry (4 registered, 3 deferred) not pinned." The Step 1 matcher-pin test pins matcher correctness; the Step 2 test pins disjointness for Step-2 fns. The triangulation of "matcher recognizes 7, registry has 4, none of the other 3 are leaked into other tiers" isn't pinned anywhere. A future contributor who pre-registers ISFORMULA as scalar (for testing) would not get caught by any existing test until Step 3 lands.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:107:**Recommendation.** Step 1 must include a sub-bullet: "Extend `is_aggregate_function_lists_only_registered_aggregates` with a third loop checking `reg.lookup_reference_aware(name).is_some()` for the new names." Also rename the matcher itself — `is_aggregate_function` is now load-bearing for THREE concepts (genuine aggregates, range-aware binding, reference-aware binding). The W5-X comment at plan.rs:359-376 already calls this out as "historical"; the design should explicitly bundle a one-shot rename to `accepts_range_arg_at_bind` or similar, even if the ParamSchema migration is deferred (§ R4).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:132:Most cleanly: ROW/COLUMN/ROWS/COLUMNS take dep-suppress treatment (option c), ISFORMULA/FORMULATEXT take new formula-status dep kind (option b deferred to a followup but tracked). v1 acceptable: option (a) for all 7, documented.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:415:4. **Implicit-intersection interaction** — `=@ROW(A1:A10)` — does the `@` wrap narrow before or after ROW evaluates? Per design § 1.2.1's deferred spill semantics, single-arg ROW returns top-left regardless; `@` should be idempotent. Pin with a test.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:519:**Detail.** The 2026-05-16 Wave 2 design (line 27) lists ADDRESS in batch 4.10.G (XLOOKUP/XMATCH+ADDRESS, status active). This new reference-tier doc § 1 "out of scope" lists `OFFSET / ADDRESS / INDIRECT`. They conflict — is ADDRESS in 4.10.G or deferred to reference-tier? Verify against actual registry HEAD.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:570:**Recommendation.** Update § 10 question 8 with the pre-365 vs Excel-365 distinction. Recommend matching IronCalc (multi-cell → `#N/A` per MEDIUM-1) as v1 — consistent with our deferred spill story (§ 8 R5).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:112:## 2. Non-goals (deferred)
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:263:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:272:| 12 | **4.9.L** (W5-148, shipped) | Round-trip + edge case verification suite. +12 end-to-end property tests in `workbook_runtime::tests`: mixed-relativity range rejection at set_formula, `Sales[@Col]` vs `@Sales[Qty]` semantic equivalence, `@A:A` / `@1:1` whole-range narrowing at anchor, `Sheet1!@A1` cross-sheet, R1C1+EN round-trip through op-log replay (set_reference_mode + set_formula both replayed), DE+EN round-trip through replay, `@` preservation through replay, reference_mode/locale changes leave stored text canonical, `@scalar` idempotency, `@SUM(scalar args)` no-op. Note: rule 7 (function-returns-array → top-left) deferred — array-returning functions in scalar context still return `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit; closing megaudit (4.9.O) decides whether to bundle that with cell-boundary spill rewiring or defer to a Phase 4.10 polish item. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:1338:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:6969:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:463:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1601:docs/known-gaps.md:81:| GAP-F-07 | `FormatTable` GC / compaction not implemented. Sparse format-overlay (Phase 4.5.D) interns format strings into a workbook-level `FormatTable`. When cells change format, the old `FormatId` entry is NOT garbage-collected. Long-lived workbooks that cycle through many formats grow the table. **Decision (W5-68 design doc § 7.5):** deferred — typical workbooks don't cycle formats; a compaction pass lands in Phase 4.10 or on explicit user request. | Filed at design time (W5-68); no code yet | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1602:docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

Significance is `abs(significance)` — sign ignored (unlike CEILING). Default significance=1, mode=0. Positive number always rounds toward +∞; negative number with mode=0 rounds toward +∞ (toward zero), with mode≠0 rounds toward -∞ (away from zero). significance=0 returns 0. CEILING.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2289:docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:124:| FLOOR.MATH | ✅ | 8 | 4.3 polish | W5-61: signature `(number, [significance], [mode])`. Mirror of CEILING.MATH. Positive number rounds toward -∞; negative+mode=0 toward -∞ (away from zero); negative+mode≠0 toward +∞ (toward zero). significance=0 + nonzero number → #DIV/0! (mirrors FLOOR canon, diverges from CEILING.MATH). FLOOR.PRECISE deferred to 4.10. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2393:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:463:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2583:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:6430:docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:177:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2585:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:6432:docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:186:| 12 | **4.9.L** (W5-148, shipped) | Round-trip + edge case verification suite. +12 end-to-end property tests in `workbook_runtime::tests`: mixed-relativity range rejection at set_formula, `Sales[@Col]` vs `@Sales[Qty]` semantic equivalence, `@A:A` / `@1:1` whole-range narrowing at anchor, `Sheet1!@A1` cross-sheet, R1C1+EN round-trip through op-log replay (set_reference_mode + set_formula both replayed), DE+EN round-trip through replay, `@` preservation through replay, reference_mode/locale changes leave stored text canonical, `@scalar` idempotency, `@SUM(scalar args)` no-op. Note: rule 7 (function-returns-array → top-left) deferred — array-returning functions in scalar context still return `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit; closing megaudit (4.9.O) decides whether to bundle that with cell-boundary spill rewiring or defer to a Phase 4.10 polish item. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2641:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:112:## 2. Non-goals (deferred)
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2642:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:263:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2645:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:272:| 12 | **4.9.L** (W5-148, shipped) | Round-trip + edge case verification suite. +12 end-to-end property tests in `workbook_runtime::tests`: mixed-relativity range rejection at set_formula, `Sales[@Col]` vs `@Sales[Qty]` semantic equivalence, `@A:A` / `@1:1` whole-range narrowing at anchor, `Sheet1!@A1` cross-sheet, R1C1+EN round-trip through op-log replay (set_reference_mode + set_formula both replayed), DE+EN round-trip through replay, `@` preservation through replay, reference_mode/locale changes leave stored text canonical, `@scalar` idempotency, `@SUM(scalar args)` no-op. Note: rule 7 (function-returns-array → top-left) deferred — array-returning functions in scalar context still return `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit; closing megaudit (4.9.O) decides whether to bundle that with cell-boundary spill rewiring or defer to a Phase 4.10 polish item. |

VERDICT: FAIL

**HIGH**

1. [repair.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/repair.rs:394): table repair is wrong after table auto-disambiguation. `collect_table_renames` keys history by the op’s requested `new_name`, not the actual post-replay table name. For `T1 -> X` and `T3 -> X`, replay produces `{X, X(2)}`, but repair stores both historic names under `"X"`. Phase 3 then emits rules like `T3 -> X`, even when `T3` is the table that actually became `X(2)`. That can rewrite `T3[B]` to `X[B]`, causing `#NAME?` or silently reading the wrong table if columns overlap. This is worse than “misses the rewrite”; it can corrupt formulas.

2. [replay.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:896): column auto-disambiguation ships without column formula repair. If peer A renames `A -> Z` and peer B renames `B -> Z`, replay can make one column `Z(2)`, but producer-side `PutFormula` ops from the suffixed peer still point at `T[Z]`. Since no column repair pass landed, those formulas can bind to the wrong column. If “column repair deferred” is accepted scope, it needs to be called out as a user-visible formula corruption limitation, not just a missing polish item.

**MEDIUM**

1. [replay.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:804): missing-source `RenameTable` now always returns `Ok(())`, including genuinely corrupt single-writer logs like `Wrong -> X` where neither table exists. The comment says “error only when there’s clearly no related table state,” but the code never errors in that branch. Same issue for columns at [replay.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:896). This may be an intentional V1 replay-robustness tradeoff, but it is broader than documented and weakens producer-validation checks.

2. [repair.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/repair.rs:419): table repair iterates a `HashSet`, so rule ordering/report ordering is nondeterministic. Sheet repair sorts sheet ids; table repair should sort current canonicals, especially because remaining ambiguous historic-name cases are already acknowledged V1 risk.

3. [replay.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-oplog/src/replay.rs:831): the NameTable check runs before TableTable availability on every suffix candidate. So yes, a defined-name collision at suffix 5 hard-errors even if the table namespace is free there. That matches your stated policy, but it leaves a hard-fail path where continuing to suffix 6 would preserve mergeability.

**LOW / TESTS**

1. [repair_tables.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/tests/repair_tables.rs:157): `step4_concurrent_same_table_rename_does_not_hard_fail` is weak and uses `T -> T` vs `T -> T2`, not the real `T -> T2` vs `T -> T3` advisory-skip case. The count assertion catches 0/2 tables, but does not pin final canonical state.

2. [repair_tables.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/tests/repair_tables.rs:1): the file header claims BatchCommit and empty/same-canonical coverage, but the file has no such tests. The recursive BatchCommit code exists; the coverage claim is false.

3. Reused-table safety test is non-overlapping. Actual original table is rows 0..1 (`rows: 2`), new `T` is rows 5..6. The assertion is valid.

4. `T[A] -> T2[A]` is correct: [rewrite_table_ref](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-formula-syntax/src/ast.rs:408) only rewrites `table_name`; the column spec remains `A`.

**Synthesis**

Step 4 fixes the immediate hard-fail class, but the repair extension is not sound once replay auto-disambiguates table names, and the column side has the same formula-corruption shape with no repair pass. The advisory skip itself is defensible as a V1 limitation, but the implementation currently makes corrupt single-writer rename ops silently disappear and the public docs/test coverage do not make that contract crisp. I would not ship this commit as closure without at least fixing table repair’s actual-name mapping for suffixes and either landing column repair or explicitly documenting/probing the column formula corruption limitation.

Step 4 fixes the immediate hard-fail class, but the repair extension is not sound once replay auto-disambiguates table names, and the column side has the same formula-corruption shape with no repair pass. The advisory skip itself is defensible as a V1 limitation, but the implementation currently makes corrupt single-writer rename ops silently disappear and the public docs/test coverage do not make that contract crisp. I would not ship this commit as closure without at least fixing table repair’s actual-name mapping for suffixes and either landing column repair or explicitly documenting/probing the column formula corruption limitation.
